verdict.summary: Demo keys and auto-populated demo companies are self-serve within an hour, but the Gusto API is restricted to App Integration and Embedded partners: production keys need an approved Production Pre-Approval, a third-party security review and a QA review of your build, and Gusto says not all applications are approved. Early-stage products without a track record serving small businesses are listed as not currently supported.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sign up, create an organization and an application with a redirect URI, then create a demo company that comes pre-filled with employees and past payrolls.

timeToProd.assumes: A direct Integrated App reading employee and payroll data, with a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report on hand; going through an approved Unified API partner still requires the same pre-approval and security review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Partnerships review of Production Pre-Approval, then the GRC security review (run with VISO Trust), then Developer Relations QA of your Partner Checklist before production keys are issued.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Gusto publishes no timeline. Finch's guide says Gusto 'typically takes at least 2 weeks to respond' to the questionnaire, the security review step takes 2–4 weeks, and there's no fast track. QA time depends on your build.

prerequisites.item: A software product serving businesses, with shared Gusto customers and an established track record
prerequisites.why: Gusto lists early-stage products and customers connecting their own systems as not currently supported.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Gusto customers connecting their own company should use the Gusto CLI or Gusto MCP server instead.

prerequisites.why: Without it Gusto won't provide implementation support, QA review or production keys.

prerequisites.item: Security documentation: SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS, pen test reports, and security and privacy policies
prerequisites.why: The pre-approval questionnaire feeds the security review; without a formal audit you answer a long list of control questions.

prerequisites.item: Users who are primary or full-access admins in Gusto
prerequisites.why: Only those admins can enable and authorize a new application for a company.

scopeTiers.tier: Demo environment (any scope you build against)
scopeTiers.impact: Demo keys only work against https://api.gusto-demo.com with demo companies.
Scopes aren't requested in the authorize URL; Gusto assigns them to your app during review based on your use case, and calls outside them are rejected in production.
Same review, but you must justify write access to payroll in your use case and demonstrate it in QA.
Benefits containing PHI are only visible with the :phi scope. Without SOC 2/ISO/PCI reports, sensitive PII such as benefits data needs a separate discussion with Gusto.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The SOC 2 requirement for benefits data comes from Finch's guide.

steps.title: Create a Developer Portal account and organization
steps.detail: Sign up, complete Organization setup, and invite teammates under Organizations > Team.

steps.title: Draft the Production Pre-Approval answers
steps.detail: Write the use case, shared-customer story, data fields needed and the security control answers, mapped to the documents you have.

steps.title: Submit Production Pre-Approval before building
steps.detail: Submit the Qualtrics application with security reports and contacts. Gusto strongly recommends approval before you invest in a build.

steps.title: Wait for pre-approval and security review
steps.detail: Partnerships reviews first; if approved, the GRC team starts the security review. Reply fast to follow-up questions or the review is put on hold.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Duration from Finch's guide, not Gusto.

steps.title: Create a demo application and demo company
steps.detail: Create an application with at least one exact redirect URI (no wildcards or fragments), copy the client_id and secret, then create a demo company.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow against demo
steps.detail: Redirect to /oauth/authorize, exchange at /oauth/token (JSON body), store tokens per company UUID, and rotate the single-use refresh token on every refresh. Use https://api.gusto-demo.com.

steps.title: Complete the Partner Checklist
steps.detail: After pre-approval you get the Partner Checklist; copy it and fill in each item from your build, including the scopes you exercise in demo.

steps.title: Submit for QA review
steps.detail: Share the completed Partner Checklist with developer@gusto.com and walk Gusto through the demo integration.

steps.title: Wait for QA and production keys
steps.detail: Developer Relations assigns scopes and issues production keys in the portal once approved. Production redirect URIs can only be changed by emailing developer@gusto.com.

steps.title: Launch and request scope changes as needed
steps.detail: Move to https://api.gusto.com. Request extra scopes by emailing developer@gusto.com. You can't test with demo accounts in production.

agentCanDo: Draft the Pre-Approval use case and security answers
Build the OAuth flow with single-use refresh token rotation
Store one grant per company and handle multi-company admins
Fill in the Partner Checklist from the build
Implement 429 backoff under 200 requests/min per grant
humanMustDo: Create the Developer Portal account and organization
Submit Production Pre-Approval with real security reports
Submit the Partner Checklist for QA
Email Gusto for production redirect or scope changes

blockers.cause: Product is early-stage, the use case doesn't map to a supported category, or it's a customer connecting their own company.
blockers.fix: Apply once you have shared customers and a track record; for internal use, use Gusto CLI or the Gusto MCP server.

blockers.symptom: Production API calls rejected for an endpoint that worked in demo
blockers.cause: The endpoint's scope wasn't assigned to your app during review.
blockers.fix: Email developer@gusto.com to request the additional scope.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with invalid_grant after a retry or race
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are single-use; the first refresh invalidated it.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes per grant and persist the new refresh token atomically.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Gusto states refresh tokens are 'invalid after one use'; the error string is our assumption.

blockers.symptom: 403 Forbidden with a token that used to work across companies
blockers.cause: Since v2023-05-01, tokens must be strict access tokens scoped to a single company.
blockers.fix: Have the admin authorize each company separately, or exchange legacy tokens with grant_type=strict_access.

blockers.cause: They aren't a primary admin or full-access admin on the Gusto company.
blockers.fix: Ask a primary or full-access admin to connect.

blockers.cause: Over 200 requests in a rolling 60-second window for one OAuth grant.
blockers.fix: Throttle per grant and back off until the window clears.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 2 hours; refresh tokens never expire but are invalid after one use, and each refresh returns a new pair.
Each OAuth grant covers exactly one company; accountants and multi-company admins must authorize every company separately.
Rate limit is 200 requests per minute per OAuth grant, on a 60-second rolling window.
Demo and production use different hosts (api.gusto-demo.com vs api.gusto.com) and different keys; test companies aren't supported in production.
Going through an approved Unified API platform doesn't skip Gusto's pre-approval and security review.
Gusto offers its own CLI and MCP server for customers connecting their own company, which is the intended path for an internal AI agent rather than a partner app.
